2610.12022.title: Examining Social Attribution in LLM Reasoning: A Theory-Guided Probing Methodology
2610.12022.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sociotechnical systems where social attribution, the reasoning process attributing external events to the causes and reasons of agents' social behaviors, plays a critical role. These processes involve judgments of social cause, responsibility, and blame/credit to agents. Although attributional models are well-studied in social psychology and cognition through Attribution Theory, social attribution remains underexplored in AI, particularly LLM social reasoning. This paper provides the first systematic exploration of LLM social attribution. Our work focuses on responsibility and blame attributions, examining current LLMs' judgments and their underlying internal mechanisms. Guided by attribution theory, we construct a social attribution benchmark consisting of a Vignette subset based on classic scenarios from attribution theory research and a Reality subset based on real-world social narratives, yielding 7,639 responsibility/blame judgment questions. On this basis, we evaluate 32 representative LLMs and 5 basic non-LLM baselines. To further explore the internal mechanisms underlying the LLM judgment process, we develop a probing-based methodology to investigate the latent-space representations of 5 key attribution dimensions and the consistency of their influences on LLM judgments compared to those in human social attribution. Our research findings reveal that current LLMs exhibit measurable but incomplete agreement with human responsibility and blame judgments, and meanwhile, this agreement is positively correlated with model size. Some attribution dimensions are systematically decodable from specific positions in LLM hidden states, and their influences on the final judgment are consistent with those indicated by human Attribution Theory. The dataset and associated code are available at https://github.com/Yuzhaoxin946/SAB-Bench.
2610.12022.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地被應用於社會技術系統中，其中社會歸因，將外部事件歸因於代理人社會行為的原因和理由的推理過程，扮演著關鍵角色。這些過程涉及對社會原因、責任以及對代理人的指責/讚譽的判斷。儘管歸因模型在社會心理學和認知科學中通過歸因理論得到了充分研究，但在人工智慧，特別是LLM社會推理中，社會歸因仍然未被充分探索。本文提供了對LLM社會歸因的首次系統性探索。我們的工作專注於責任和指責的歸因，檢視當前LLMs的判斷及其潛在的內部機制。在歸因理論的指導下，我們構建了一個社會歸因基準，包含基於經典歸因理論研究場景的Vignette子集和基於現實社會敘事的Reality子集，產生了7,639個責任/指責判斷問題。在此基礎上，我們評估了32個代表性的LLMs和5個基本的非LLM基準。為了進一步探索LLM判斷過程中潛在的內部機制，我們開發了一種基於探測的研究方法，調查5個關鍵歸因維度的潛在空間表示及其對LLM判斷的影響與人類社會歸因的比較一致性。我們的研究結果顯示，當前的LLMs在責任和指責判斷上與人類的可測量但不完全一致，並且這種一致性與模型大小呈正相關。一些歸因維度可以系統性地從LLM隱藏狀態的特定位置解碼，其對最終判斷的影響與人類歸因理論所指示的一致。數據集和相關代碼可在https://github.com/Yuzhaoxin946/SAB-Bench獲得。
